record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Finite complete indicator systems for conjugacy
record.original_question: For the topological conjugacy classification of QSOs, an indicator is a polynomial in the heredity coefficients whose bounded range is forced by topological conjugacy, and a complete system of indicators is one whose bounds imply topological conjugacy. Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators for QSOs, and if so, what is a basis, meaning a minimal complete system, for these indicators?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ be the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(Vx)_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the heredity coefficients $P_{ij,k}$ satisfy $P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k} \ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i,j$. Two QSOs $V_1, V_2$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h : S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ with $h\circ V_1 = V_2\circ h$.

Call a polynomial $f$ in the variables $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ an indicator (for topological conjugacy of QSOs) if topological conjugateness of any two QSOs $V_1$ and $V_2$, with heredity coefficient arrays $P^{(1)}$ and $P^{(2)}$ respectively, forces the values $f(P^{(1)})$ and $f(P^{(2)})$ to lie in a common bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$ (equivalently, the range of $f$ on each topological-conjugacy class is bounded). A family $\mathcal F$ of indicators is called a complete system of indicators if, whenever every $f \in \mathcal F$ satisfies the corresponding bound on two QSOs $V_1, V_2$, the operators $V_1$ and $V_2$ are topologically conjugate. A minimal (under inclusion) complete system of indicators is called a basis.

Question: Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators for QSOs on $S^{m-1}$? If yes, exhibit a basis (a minimal complete system of indicators).
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this classification problem was located. Web searches on indicators and topological conjugacy of quadratic stochastic operators return only general background on QSOs and topological conjugacy and recent unrelated classification work (e.g., diagonal operators on Banach spaces, conjugacy testing for time series); none address the existence of a finite complete system of indicators or its basis for QSOs. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum analogues of quadratic stochastic operators are studied; no finite indicator basis for the classical topological conjugacy classification is mentioned.
status_evidence.claim: Survey/extension work on QSOs does not record a resolution of the indicator-basis problem.

status_evidence.title: Testing Topological Conjugacy of Time Series
status_evidence.snippet: Develops tests for topological conjugacy of trajectories of dynamical systems in general settings.
status_evidence.claim: General conjugacy-testing literature does not address the specific QSO indicator basis problem.

status_evidence.title: Topologically conjugate classification of diagonal operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies topological conjugacy classification for diagonal operators on Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent conjugacy-classification results are in unrelated settings and do not solve the QSO indicator problem.
